joel-cam-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-02.question: In Joel 2:28, tap the word that marks the later time of the promise.
joel-cam-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-02.feedbackCorrect: The promise of the Spirit comes after the announced restoration.

feedbackWrong.a: "toda" shows the scope, not the moment of the promise.
feedbackWrong.c: "sobre" shows on whom, not the moment of the promise.

joel-cam-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-02.hint: Look for the time word right at the start.

joel-cam-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-03.question: How does Joel 2:13 explain why the people can return to God?
joel-cam-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-03.feedbackCorrect: God is patient and kind, so returning makes sense.

feedbackWrong.a: Active love is the opposite of indifference in this text.
feedbackWrong.c: He calls the people to himself, showing he is very present.
feedbackWrong.d: He is slow to anger, not quick to shut doors.

joel-cam-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-03.hint: Read God's qualities in the second half.

options.a: His indifference makes the heart unnecessary
options.b: His patience and love open the way back
options.c: His distance makes returning useless
options.d: His haste to punish shuts the way back

joel-cam-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-04.question: How does Joel's thread move from loss to promise?
joel-cam-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-04.feedbackCorrect: From the loss described, the book moves to the call and restoration.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the loss in Joel 1, before the call.

joel-cam-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-04.hint: Follow the order of the book's major moments.

options.a: A plague devours the land in a chain
options.b: God calls the people to the heart
options.c: God promises to restore the years

joel-cam-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-05.question: In Joel 1:6, how is the nation that came against the land described?
joel-cam-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-05.feedbackCorrect: Mighty and without number is how the invader is presented.

feedbackWrong.a: The text says the opposite about the size of this force.
feedbackWrong.b: The force ravages the land; it does not pass without a trace.

joel-cam-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-05.hint: Read the two adjectives given to the invading nation.

joel-cam-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-06.question: What links Joel 2:13 to Psalm 51:17?
joel-cam-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-06.feedbackCorrect: God does not despise a broken and contrite heart.

feedbackWrong.a: Joel asks for the heart, not clothing as proof of return.
feedbackWrong.c: Both texts refuse to trade the inner for the outer.

joel-cam-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-06.hint: See what God does not despise in the Psalm.

options.a: Torn clothes impress God
options.c: Outward gestures replace the inner

joel-cam-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-07.question: In Joel 1:3, tap the final destination of the memory to be told.
joel-cam-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-07.feedbackCorrect: The memory passes through children and reaches the next generation.

feedbackWrong.a: That is the call to tell, not the memory's final destination.
feedbackWrong.c: Children are a link in the chain, not the final destination.

joel-cam-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-07.hint: Look for the end of the chain of passing it on.

joel-cam-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-08.question: How do the steps of Joel 1:2–3 connect?
joel-cam-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-08.feedbackCorrect: Hearing, telling the children and passing it on, in that order.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the call to hear, addressed to the elders.

joel-cam-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-08.hint: Hearing comes before telling and passing it on.

options.a: The elders hear what happened
options.b: Parents tell the event to their children
options.c: Children pass it on to the next generation

joel-pro-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-01.question: In Joel 2:29, the male and female servants also receive the Spirit poured out by God.
joel-pro-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-01.feedbackCorrect: Including the servants is part of the broad promise itself.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread 2:29 and who the word also adds.

joel-pro-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-01.hint: See who the promise's second verse includes.

joel-pro-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-02.question: In Joel 2:25, tap what God calls the plague that ate the years.
joel-pro-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-02.feedbackCorrect: The plague is presented as under God's rule and sending.

feedbackWrong.b: Years are what was eaten, not the name for the plague.
feedbackWrong.c: That gives the target of the sending, not the plague's name.

joel-pro-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-02.hint: Look for the name God gives those who devoured.

joel-pro-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-03.question: Which reading best brings together Joel's loss, call and promise?
joel-pro-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-03.feedbackCorrect: Joel links judgment, sincere return, restoration and the Spirit.

feedbackWrong.b: Sons and male and female servants rule out a restricted gift.
feedbackWrong.c: The heart is asked for instead of a merely outward gesture.
feedbackWrong.d: The promise leads to praise, not guaranteed wealth.

joel-pro-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-03.hint: Combine Joel 1, the call of 2:13 and the promises.

options.a: Judgment calls to the heart and God restores
options.b: The Spirit stays only with leaders
options.c: Outward ritual is enough without the heart

joel-pro-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-04.question: Which sequence reveals the path of the book of Joel?
joel-pro-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-04.feedbackCorrect: From loss to a turned heart, the book reaches the Spirit for all.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the loss that opens the book of Joel.

joel-pro-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-04.hint: Go from the plague to the call and the greatest promise.

options.a: Loss reveals how serious the judgment is
options.c: The Spirit is poured out on all

joel-pro-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-05.question: In Joel 2:11, who will be able to do what before the Day of the Lord?
joel-pro-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-05.feedbackCorrect: The text's question shows the unbearable weight of that Day.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not speak of escaping, but of enduring the Day.
feedbackWrong.c: Ignoring is the opposite of the attention Joel asks of the people.

joel-pro-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-05.hint: Read the question that closes the whole verse.

joel-pro-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-06.question: What links Joel 2:28 to Acts 2:17?
joel-pro-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-06.feedbackCorrect: Peter explains Pentecost with the words of the prophet Joel.

feedbackWrong.a: Acts presents the event as Joel's word fulfilled there.
feedbackWrong.b: The quotation repeats the reach to all flesh, without cuts.

joel-pro-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-06.hint: See how Peter introduces the quotation in Acts.

options.a: A promise with no prophetic word
options.c: Peter quotes Joel at Pentecost

joel-pro-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-07.question: In Joel 2:27, tap the final promise made to God's people.
joel-pro-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-07.feedbackCorrect: God's presence in their midst removes his people's shame.

feedbackWrong.b: That shows where God is, not the final promise cited.
feedbackWrong.c: That states who God is, not the final promise to the people.

joel-pro-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-07.hint: Read the last statement made about the people.

joel-pro-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-08.question: Which sequence reveals the reach of the Spirit's promise?
joel-pro-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-08.feedbackCorrect: From the total reach, the text gets to the included servants.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the widest reach, stated in 2:28.

joel-pro-joel-joel-03-desafio-joel-08.hint: Go from 2:28 to the addition in 2:29.

options.a: The Spirit on all flesh
options.c: Male and female servants also receive
